newsitem.title: UK: Unichem seeks to buy 100 pharmacies in '97.
newsitem.headline: Unichem seeks to buy 100 pharmacies in '97.

text.p: British drug wholesaler and retailer Unichem Plc said on Wednesday that it hoped to add around 100 pharmacies to its Moss chemists retail chain in 1997.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive Jeffery Harris said "we have the management team at Moss to handle that, and the opportunties because there are a lot more pharmacies coming to the market now that Lloyds has been settled." In January, the group lost a bruising tussle with German wholesaler Gehe AG for control of Lloyds Chemists Plc, which owned more than 900 British pharmacies.

Unichem's Moss Chemist chain totalled 459 stores at the end of 1996, an increase of 41 stores during the year, putting it well behind the enlarged Gehe's 1,260 strong chain and Boots Co Plc's 1,200 stores.
Harris said the acquisitions would be made on a "piecemeal basis", which would allow Unichem to pick stores that fit its requirements.
He said the group was targeting community pharmacies with a strong focus on prescpription and over-the counter drug sales.
